neighbours.label: a preposition marking the stretch of text on one side of the cursor in editor or keyboard instructions ('everything before/after the cursor'); 'elif' in Python fires more weakly
fire: In nano, pressing CTRL+k cuts all the text after the cursor on that line.
The shortcut Alt+Backspace erases the word just before the cursor.
Typing in insert mode places new characters right before the cursor.
In most shells, CTRL+u clears everything to the left of and before the cursor.
When you press End, the editor jumps past any text after the cursor.
Use Shift+Home to select the whole line before the cursor.
The terminal keeps whatever was typed after the cursor when you paste.
Pressing Delete removes one character after the cursor, not before it.
quiet: In nano, pressing CTRL+k after saving the file cuts the current line.
The shortcut Alt+Backspace was added to the editor before version two.
Typing in insert mode was common long before modern word processors.
In most shells, CTRL+u clears the line; run it before pressing Enter.
When you press End after lunch, the report editor saves your work.
Use Shift+Home before the meeting to prepare the slides quickly.
The terminal keeps the history file after the session ends.
Pressing Delete removes the file after a confirmation dialog appears.
